summary: The AURA system is an interactive, autonomous platform for monitoring crew health and managing risks during long-duration interplanetary expeditions. The architectural backbone of the project is formed by NASA’s five official space-related hazards, which directly link external environmental conditions to the physiological state of astronauts. A clickable body map shows each astronaut’s condition, from heart rate and sleep to bone density, muscle mass, vision, and radiation exposure. A mission timeline shows how those readings change over time, and rule-based alerts flag early warning signs.Spaceflight puts the body under stress that Earth-based medicine doesn’t face. AURA turns scattered readings into a clear picture of each astronaut’s risk, showing what is changing, which body system is affected, and what is causing it. It is significant because on long missions, communication delays mean crews and doctors can’t always respond in real time. A tool that spots risks early and explains them helps teams act sooner, protects astronaut health, and supports safer deep-space exploration. AURA turns complex crew health data into a clear, early picture of risk, helping teams act before problems become critical. By making astronaut health easier to understand and monitor, it supports safer, longer missions beyond Earth.
details:
Our website helps astronauts monitor their health. It features a human body silhouette that users can click on to view possible symptoms and receive recommendations.

Not all astronauts have sufficient medical knowledge to identify health problems or determine appropriate solutions. Therefore, our website is designed to help them better understand their health and take appropriate action.

We used a human body model because we believe it is a more effective, intuitive, and simple way to present health information.

Our health website has a game-like design, making the experience more interactive and engaging for users.

Technologies and tools used:

AI tools: Codex, Gemini, NotebookLM

Programming languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, CSS

Other technologies: Dockerfile
dataRefs: Helps to understand that living in space requires more than advanced technology. We must also create a healthy environment that helps astronauts stay physically strong, mentally healthy, and connected to life on Earth.

Space exploration can create serious challenges for astronauts' vision and neurological health. Understanding SANS and researching possible preventive methods, such as vitamin B supplements, can help NASA protect astronauts during future missions to the Moon and Mars.

Space radiation is an invisible but serious danger to astronauts. Understanding its effects on the human body helps NASA develop better protection systems and safer conditions for long-term missions to the Moon and Mars.
Gives us an understanding of how pressure changes affect the human body helps us develop better protection systems and keep astronauts safe during long-term space missions.

Serves as the primary architectural backbone of the AURA system. It links 5 key risk factors (radiation, gravity, isolation, distance, and confined environment) to their impact on vulnerable anatomical zones on the Body Map.
